representation: A two-panel utility graph: a total-utility line above and marginal-utility bars below, sharing a movable consumption marker and a marginal-utility threshold line.
motion: the consumption marker slides across both panels
the total line stays above while the marginal bars shrink
controls: consumption slider q from 1 to 6 units
checkpoints: watch marginal fall while total rises
read the decision threshold without claiming total must fall
misconceptionTest: The bars are explicitly defined as MU(q) = U(q) - U(q-1), not as total utility. As q increases, the bars shrink from 8.4 to 0.4 while the total line keeps rising and flattens; this shows diminishing marginal utility without total utility falling. The MU = 2 line is framed as a stopping rule, not a law.
accessibility: Both panels have text labels, the marker and threshold are labeled in the surrounding copy, the slider is keyboard accessible, and alt text gives the direction of both series.
